19 Apr 2017 · Paper · Scientific Reports 7, 46421

Increased spontaneous MEG signal diversity for psychoactive doses of ketamine, LSD and psilocybin

Schartner MM, Carhart-Harris RL, Barrett AB, Seth AK, Muthukumaraswamy SD

Psychedelics pushed brain-signal diversity above normal waking levels, the first time such measures went higher than wakefulness.

Complexity scores are usually highest in normal waking. Under psilocybin, ketamine and LSD they went higher still, and some of the rise tracked how intense people said the experience was.

Spontaneous MEG; LZ and entropy measures higher for all three drugs, even when controlling for spectral changes; strongest for single-channel LZ (temporal diversity). Selective correlations with phenomenological intensity ratings.

What we do with it

Tests whether a measure rises when contents intensify but level does not obviously change. We re-check the spectral control with phase-randomised surrogates. Planned

Read the original. Source checked against the original.
